answer: Work history stays time-locked, so credit unlocks only after the epoch closes and only if independent auditors sign the same record. The design cannot stop a patient farm from aging 200 accounts in parallel. It can make that farm pay, because each record needs a quorum spanning unrelated subnetworks, so 200 accounts age in 200 places. An atlas of accounts held in one harbor resolves to one region and fails the quorum. An opal badge bought today proves nothing until the lock matures, which parks a farm's capital for four epochs before its first payout.
